description: Club de Ciencias del Colegio San Ignacio
summary: We developed a videogame idea called Outpost Zer0 about building an outpost on the Moon. The game starts with the user being on a rocket, which is almost out of fuel, returning to Earth . To survive, the user's crew and the user will have to land on the Moon and build and outpost until help from Earth arrives. The game will explain certain concepts, such as radiation and solar panel energy in an easy way so that the kids who play it can actually understand their meaning. While being on the Moon, the user will face missions related to the survival of the crew and the functioning of the outpost so that they can truly understand the hard decisions that have to be made on a lunar mission. This game will allow children to learn scientific and complex concepts in an understandable way.
details:
The game dynamic

The game starts when the screen shows a message: “You are in a rocket, coming back to Earth from a space mission on a far away planet alongside your team”. Under this message, the three characters that are part of the user’s team will appear: Harper (woman) (blue suit), Arthur (man) (pink suit) and John (man) (green suit). The previous message disappears and a new message appears: “However, the rocket is suddenly almost out of fuel. The Moon is close enough for a safe landing, but your teammate John assures you the rocket is capable of making it to Earth. As the crew’s leader, you have to choose what to do”. The previous message disappears  and a new message appears: “Choose what to do”. Under this message, two buttons with the two options will appear:

Option 1: “Try making it to Earth”

If the user picks this option, the screen will show the rocket trying to reach Earth but in the end, it will be unable to do it . A message appears on the screen: “On the way back, the rocket runs completely out of fuel and the communication with the Earth’s space base is cut off. The rocket is stranded in space with no way back”. The previous message disappears and a new message appears: “Game Over”, over a button that says: “Try again”. When the user presses the button, it will lead them back to the screen with the two previous options: “Try making it to Earth” and “Land on the Moon”. The “Try making it to Earth” button will flicker a couple times and then turn off, making the option unavailable.

Option 2: “Land on the Moon”

If the user picks this option, the screen will show the rocket landing safely on the Moon, but a bar showing how much fuel the rocket has left will be completely empty. A message appears that says: “You and your crew have managed to reach the moon safely, but your rocket is officially out of fuel”. The previous message disappears and a new message appears: “After talking with the Earth’s space base and communicating your problem through the radio, your superiors tell you that help will not be able to get there soon, and you’ll have to build and outpost with your crew to ensure your survival while you wait”. The inside of the rocket is shown, with the whole crew inside having an indistinctive conversation. A new message is shown over this image: “After discussing it with your crew, you’ve decided to explore the Moon’s terrain to find a proper place for the outpost". The screen shows a message that says “DAY 1” and then disappears so the screen becomes playable for the user (the player is able to enter the rocket). On the screen there are three bars: 

-BAR 1: A green bar that shows radiation. When it's full, the user loses because it dies of radiation. The user's suit helps keep it down when exploring the Moon’s terrain, making the bar get full slower. But when the user is in the outpost it will be safe from radiation.

-BAR 2: A blue bar that shows oxygen levels. When the user is exploring the Moon’s terrain, the oxygen bar will get empty very slowly. When the user is in the outpost, the oxygen bar will slowly get full again. 

-BAR 3: A red bar that shows hunger. After a while the bar will get slowly empty, and to fill it the user must eat the food from the outpost.

While exploring the terrain the user will find an arrow pointing towards a Moon’s rock. When the user gets close enough to it, a message appears: “Congratulations! You’ve found regolith, a material that you can use to build your outpost and protect it from radiation. Radiation is the transmission of energy through space, which in these conditions can be very harmful for you”. The user will need to find more regolith to then build its outpost with its team’s help, this will cause the user to lose some oxygen, be a little hungry. After building the outpost, the user and the crew will be able to enter it. When the outpost is finally built there will be a fourth bar, specifically for the outpost:

-BAR 4: A yellow bar that shows energy. After a while the bar will get slowly empty, but it will get empty faster if the user uses the outpost functions. The solar panels that fuel the energy generator will need maintenance one in a while, which will cost oxygen and hunger.

Every day, the user will be able to accept or reject missions. These missions will allow the user to explore the Moon and face hard choices like in a real space mission.

The game graphic design

Outpost Zer0 would be a 2D game, with a simple but appealing pixel art design. The outpost on the inside will have white walls and panels with colorful buttons and flickering lights. On the left side there will be an energy generator with a sign of a lightning. On the right side, there will be a food reserve to recharge the hunger bar. On the outside, the outpost will have a few solar panels. The rocket will be next to the outpost, on the inside the rocket will have white walls with a lot of panels and buttons, like an actual spaceship. On one side there will be four grey sleeping bags attached to the walls of the rocket, one for each member of the crew.
